title: Private Credit Risks Explained, Oil Surges Above $100 | The Weekly Wrap
summary: Eisman separates war-driven inflation risk from AI capital returns and private-credit stress. He distinguishes retail fund liquidity from underlying credit quality, but overstates the absence of prior credit cycles and treats SoFi securitization access as indispensable despite its deposit-funded bank. Software refinancing and related-party asset transfers are material concerns whose magnitude remains unresolved. He endorses transparency and incentive reform in drug pricing without endorsing price controls.
assessment: Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman is the sole substantive speaker; viewer questions are distinguished from his responses.
framework_points: Separate liquidity constraints from realized credit losses.
Follow fast credit growth and sector concentrations.
Stress the financing waterfall rather than just headline asset value.
Distinguish AI supplier spending from eventual investor returns.
Demand transparency in both credit marks and healthcare incentives.
tools_and_charts: Private-credit market growth and software exposure
PBM rebates and Cost Plus markup
transcript_cautions: Opening montage repeats later statements and is not separately counted.
Caption names Treasury Secretary Mnuchin; contemporary identity needs checking before attribution.
MFS is called MFS Investment Management here, whereas the March 6 episode identifies Market Financial Solutions; do not transfer fraud allegations to the unrelated asset manager.
SoFi illustrative 10%/5% rates are annualized yields, despite monthly wording.
Viewer drug-pricing argument is a question, not automatically Eisman endorsement.

claims.claim: The US has had no credit cycle of any kind since the GFC and is therefore overdue for one.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Use his definition of rising loan losses and inspect post-GFC credit-loss series; elapsed time alone does not establish imminence.
claims.reason: His literal no-cycle claim conflicts with multiple post-GFC increases in bank credit-card charge-off rates. A lack of another GFC is a different claim.

evidence.title: Large bank consumer credit card net charge-off rate
evidence.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia / FRED
evidence.finding: Quarterly series rises from 2.99% in 2015Q3 to 5.03% in 2020Q2, and from 1.93% in 2021Q4 to 6.01% in 2025Q1. This contradicts literally no post-GFC episode of increasing loan losses, without establishing a systemic crisis.

evidence.title: SoFi first-quarter 2026 reported financial results
evidence.finding: Q1 deposits $40.2bn; average deposits exceeded 90% of average liabilities. Originations $12.2bn. SCLP securitizations support loan-platform partners, one funding channel among deposits, loan sales and others.

evidence.title: SoFi SCLP 2025-1 closing announcement
evidence.finding: SCLP 2025-1 was a co-contributor deal primarily involving collateral previously placed with loan-platform partners. Notes $697.6m. SoFi Bank is a nationally chartered bank; exposure cannot be inferred solely from loan origination branding.
